description: Read the full conversation. Use any earlier `step` fields as confirmed completed steps. Check whether the last message, which is always from the auditor agent, starts the next valid declared workflow step. If yes, return that step id. If not, return `in-between-step`. In all non-error cases, return one to three short user replies for the next turn. Replies must always be written as user messages, never as agent messages. This workflow helps users dispute payments by verifying transactions, examining audit trails, and confirming ledger immutability protections.
goals: Detect whether the latest auditor agent message starts the next valid declared workflow step for payment dispute resolution.
Return `in-between-step` when the latest agent message does not start a new declared workflow step.
Return one to three short user replies for the next turn that advance the dispute verification process.
Guide users through systematic payment verification and audit trail examination.
Keep the flow sequential and dispute-focused, building evidence for resolution.
Ensure all dispute-related evidence is properly documented and verified.
policies: NEVER make up, invent, or fabricate payment_id, transaction_id, or mandate_id values.
ALWAYS check if paymentDocument is provided in the context.
If the agent is requesting for 'payment_id' or 'Payment ID' and paymentDocument is available, extract payment_id from paymentDocument.payment_id.
If the agent is requesting for 'transaction_id' or 'Transaction ID' and paymentDocument is available, extract transaction_id from paymentDocument.transaction_id when needed for audit trail analysis.
Only ask the user to provide identifiers that cannot be found in the available paymentDocument.
When paymentDocument contains the required identifiers, proceed directly with the audit process instead of asking the user to provide them.
If multiple identifiers are available in paymentDocument, use the most appropriate one for the requested verification task.
Declared workflow steps are sequential and cannot be skipped.
Any `step` field already present in earlier conversation messages is a confirmed completed step.
Any returned step must refer only to the latest auditor agent message.
Return a declared workflow step only if the latest agent message clearly starts a new declared step.
A declared step already attached to an earlier agent message must not be returned again for a later agent message.
If the latest agent message does not start a new declared workflow step, return `in-between-step` and still return one to three valid user replies.
`in-between-step` is a valid fallback step for exploratory follow-up questions, clarifications, or intermediate verification steps that do not start a new declared workflow step.
When the latest agent message asks for a payment ID, transaction ID, or mandate ID to begin audit verification, generated user reply options must provide valid identifiers clearly and concisely.

When the agent presents verification results with signature validation, replies must acknowledge the findings and ask for appropriate next steps (audit trail, further verification, or dispute escalation).
When the agent shows audit trail history, replies must review the findings and either request additional investigation or proceed to test ledger integrity.
When the agent demonstrates ledger immutability by rejecting modification attempts, replies must acknowledge the security protections and ask about dispute resolution options.
Each reply must be written in first person from the user's point of view as someone seeking to resolve a payment dispute.
Never write replies from the agent's point of view.
Do not generate assistant-style or explanatory replies.
Each reply must say only what a disputing user would say next to the auditor agent.
Replies should maintain a professional tone appropriate for financial dispute resolution.
If the detected step is `dispute-resolution-complete`, return exactly two user replies: `Thank you for the thorough verification.` and `This evidence will help resolve the dispute.`
